family: Orders ended by a class-wide event: NIRA Title I orders (X1 type nra_code_approval), Canal Zone orders (canal_zone) and Philippine orders (philippines)

mechanisms.description: NIRA section 2(c), as amended by section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935): Title I 'shall cease to be in effect and any agencies established hereunder shall cease to exist' on April 1, 1936. A lapse of authority does not by itself end an order (ruling P3). The statute's words do end two kinds of member: an order whose only content is a delegation of Title I powers, which has nothing left to exercise once the Title's provisions cease (ruling P8), and an order whose only subject is an agency established under Title I (ruling P7). Every other Title I order is reached through EO 7076 (M2).
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Fixed: April 1, 1936 at the latest; an earlier end (own terms, a later order, the June 14, 1935 repeal of code provisions) controls when shown.

mechanisms.description: EO 7076 (June 15, 1935), an express class instrument (ruling P3): it ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation, and also to extend the authority and activities of any agency created thereunder until April 1, 1936', subject to earlier limitation or cancellation and without any code-approval or code-enforcement power. A member issued under Title I before June 15, 1935 is placed in that class by its own authority clause and date.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to April 1, 1936.

mechanisms.description: S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (June 14, 1935) repealed every Title I provision 'delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes'. This is a repeal of authority: under ruling P3 it is a disclosed earlier candidate end for code-dependent commands, not an end, and no branch dates a lead by it.

Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States (May 27, 1935) and Panama Refining Co. v. Ryan (January 7, 1935) held the section 3 code-making delegation and the section 9(c) petroleum delegation unconstitutional. They are recorded as validity characterizations, not end dates; no branch dates an end by them.

EO 7075 section 1 (June 15, 1935): 'The National Industrial Recovery Board created by Executive Order No. 6859 ... is hereby terminated'. It abolishes by name the only subject of EO 6859 and EO 6993 (ruling P7).

EO 6771 (June 30, 1934) ordered the National Recovery Review Board, which it identifies as established 'by Executive Order of March 7, 1934', discontinued 'prior to July 1, 1934' and that it 'shall cease to exist on that date' (ruling P7 for EO 6632; EO 6771's own only command ends on the same date).

EO 7252 (December 21, 1935, effective January 1, 1936): section 1 terminated 'The National Recovery Administration and the office of Administrator thereof'; section 2 transferred 'The Division of Review, the Division of Business Cooperation, and the Advisory Council, as constituted by Executive Order No. 7075 of June 15, 1935' to Commerce and directed the Secretary 'to terminate the functions and duties of the said agencies not later than April 1, 1936'.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: January 1, 1936 (office of Administrator) to April 1, 1936 (divisions).

mechanisms.description: Single act on issue (own terms). An order whose only operative content revokes another order, or dismisses a complaint, does one thing when it issues and is spent (ruling P1). An order whose only operative content amends other orders merges into the parents on issue (ruling P2): its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. An order whose operative content is one act for one named person follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON instead (ruling P4).
EO 7076's only operative content amends the existing Title I orders; under ruling P2 it merges into them on issue (June 15, 1935), and its extension to April 1, 1936 lives and ends with them.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Order date (June 15, 1935); the amended orders ended by April 1, 1936.

mechanisms.description: Express revocation, rescission, repeal or supersession by a later held order that names the member by number or by its date and subject: EO 7234 (November 25, 1935) revoked EO 2040 and EO 3761; EO 6064 (March 3, 1933) rescinded EO 5143; EO 6344 (October 20, 1933) superseded and revoked EO 6223; EO 6575 (January 24, 1934) revoked EO 6237; EO 4006 (May 7, 1924) rescinded EO 3985; EO 2907 (July 9, 1918) superseded EO 2867; EO 393 (January 12, 1906) repealed 'Executive Order of November 15, 1905, as to appointments to positions in the service of the Isthmian Canal Commission upon the Isthmus of Panama' (EO 370). An express class revocation also reaches its members (ruling P3): EO 3027 (January 25, 1919), 'All Executive Orders heretofore issued for the establishment of Defensive Sea Areas are hereby revoked', reaches EO 2692, 'Establishing Defensive Sea Areas for Terminal Ports of the Panama Canal'.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Fixed: the acting order's date, read from its held text.

mechanisms.description: End of the Canal Zone (ruling P5). The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force October 1, 1979: it terminated the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)), the Canal Zone Government ceased to operate in Panama (art. III(10)) and Panama reassumed plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone (art. XI(1)). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 did not end Zone rules: it continued them 'for the purpose of the exercise by the United States of law enforcement and judicial jurisdiction during the transition period' (sec. 2101) and re-read 'Canal Zone' as the areas made available to the United States under the Treaty 'and related agreements' (sec. 3(b)). The end therefore rests on the Treaty: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999' (art. II(2)); 22 U.S.C. 3602(d) calls that day the Canal Transfer Date. Under ruling P5 that termination is the latest bound for Canal Zone orders. The Treaty and 22 U.S.C. 3602(d) are not yet held.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to December 31, 1999 (outer bound); civil government functions ended October 1, 1979 and transition-period court and police jurisdiction 30 months later, but this doctrine does not date members inside the interval.

mechanisms.description: Philippine independence (ruling P5). Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act (48 Stat. 456, 463) directed the President to 'withdraw and surrender all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty then existing and exercised by the United States in and over the territory and people of the Philippine Islands, including all military and other reservations ... (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 (July 4, 1946, 60 Stat. 1352, 1353), acting 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', declared that 'The United States of America hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised by the United States of America in and over the territory and people of the Philippines'. Those words describe a class, every right of U.S. supervision, jurisdiction or control over the Islands, that an order directing U.S. supervision of the Islands' government falls in. The excepted reservations are not reached by M12. Section 7 of the Act, which governs the Commonwealth period and the High Commissioner, opens 'Until the final and complete withdrawal of American sovereignty'.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval: from the order's date to July 4, 1946.

mechanisms.description: Delegation of a statutory power that ceased (ruling P8). When a member's only content delegates powers that Title I conferred, NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended ('This title shall cease to be in effect ... on April 1, 1936') leaves the delegation nothing to exercise after that date.

not.text_regex: (authority|powers?)( and discretion)?( thereby)? (vested in|conferred (up)?on) me.{0,350}?(title II\b|titles I and II|section 20[0-9]|Public,? No\.? 5\b|March 31, 1933|Deficiency Act|Agricultural Adjustment|Federal Emergency Relief|Emergency Appropriation Act|Emergency Relief Appropriation|Public Resolution (No\.? )?44|joint resolution approved June 19, 1934|Reconstruction Finance|Federal Trade Commission|Code of the District of Columbia|Bituminous Coal Conservation)|aforesaid legislation|statutes aforesaid|said Acts of Congress|an agency, to wit:? a (banking )?corporation|hereby allocated|section 2[0-2][0-9] of the National Industrial Recovery Act|directed to (allot|make available)

lead.basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

date_rule.basis: EO 7076; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended by S.J. Res. 113 sec. 1

gaps: EO 7076 is held only as a mirror transcription.
Orders citing Title I 'and otherwise' may rest partly on unnamed general authority; EO 7076 reaches them because they were issued under Title I.
The authority-clause test is a text pattern: it reads the 350 characters after 'authority vested in me'.

procedure.description: NRA-typed orders whose text is only an amendment of another Title I order and does not act for one named person (EO 6612-A amending EO 6580).

when.text_regex: ^(Paragraph numbered \d+ of )?Executive Order No\. ?\d+\S*[^.]{0,160}? is hereby amended

not.text_regex: titles I and II|title II\b|hereby established

lead.basis: The member's own text shows that amending another Title I order is its only operative content. Its text merged into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it (coordinator ruling P2).

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. Parent: EO 6580 (branch N6, ended by 1936-04-01).
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, the lead becomes open pending the parent (ruling P2).

procedure.description: Canal Zone appointments or designations of named persons (Isthmian Canal Commission members, Canal Zone justices, special judges).

lead.basis: One-person order; follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (coordinator ruling P4). The appointment is spent when the person takes office and the person's tenure is a surviving consequence; PD-CS-ONE-PERSON's members are selected by other X1 types, so its rule does not yet reach these orders.

gaps: Needs PD-CS-ONE-PERSON's rule for appointments.
Stated ends disclosed, not applied: EO 4087 designates James W. Blackburn special judge 'until Jan. 1, 1926', EO 4567 'until Jan. 1, 1928', EO 4767 'until Jan. 1, 1929' (WPA summaries).
Tenures not traced; the Isthmian Canal Commission's discontinuance under the Panama Canal Act of August 24, 1912 (37 Stat. 560) is not held.
EO 1320 and EO 577½ name persons who appear in later orders.

procedure.description: Canal Zone orders that only revoke another order.

lead.basis: The member's own text shows that revoking another order is its only operative content; the command is exhausted on issue, and its consequence belongs to the revoked order's lifecycle (coordinator ruling P1).

gaps: The revoked order's own end is recorded in its lifecycle, not here.

procedure.description: Canal Zone orders that only amend another order and do not act for one named person (the consulting engineers' allowance wording; a typographical correction).

lead.basis: The member's own text shows that amending another order is its only operative content. Its text merged into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it (coordinator ruling P2).

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. Parents: EO 348-C (open, O2b) for EO 373-A and EO 412; EO 2692 (branch R8, revoked 1919-01-25 by EO 3027) for EO 2737.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (ruling P2).

procedure.description: Canal Zone government orders confined to the Zone, whose whole text is read (Zone courts' jurisdiction, Zone usury rule, Governor's powers within Zone territory and waters).

when.text_regex: for the Canal Zone|Canal Zone Government|courts of the Canal Zone|territory and waters of the Canal Zone

not.text_regex: TRUNCATED|Panama Rail ?road|cities of Panama|city of Panama|Col[oó]n|Republic of Panama|civil[- ]service|Schedule [AB]\b|compensation|salary|annuit|estates?\b|Washington office|office in Washington|appoint

lead.basis: The member's operative content governs the Canal Zone only. Its end rests on ruling P5 and the Panama Canal Treaty: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999' (art. II(2)), after which no area answering to 'Canal Zone' remained; 22 U.S.C. 3602(d) names that day the Canal Transfer Date. The Panama Canal Act of 1979 did not end Zone rules: it continued them for transition-period law enforcement and courts (sec. 2101) and re-read 'Canal Zone' as the treaty areas (sec. 3(b)), so it only confines them within the Treaty's life. The lead is the interval (order date, 1999-12-31].

date_rule.basis: Panama Canal Treaty art. II(2), the latest bound for Canal Zone orders (ruling P5); 22 U.S.C. 3602(d)

gaps: The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 and 22 U.S.C. 3602(d) are not yet held; both were read on the web only and are listed in FETCH_PROPOSED.jsonl. Acquire them before adopting these leads.

Disclosed earlier candidates, not dated: October 1, 1979 for Zone civil government (Treaty art. III(10)); the end of the 30-month transition period for courts and police; supersession by later Zone orders; the Canal Zone Code (76A Stat. 1).

EO 2907 delegates Espionage Act title II sec. 1 powers that depend on a declared national emergency (a war-emergency predicate with its own lifecycle, PD-WAR-EMERGENCY), and Panama Canal Act sec. 3302(a) struck the second paragraph of 50 U.S.C. 191 and the words ', the Canal Zone,'; both are earlier candidate ends.

procedure.description: Philippine orders on U.S. supervision of the Islands' government (Governor General's reports; High Commissioner's functions for the Commonwealth).

when.text_regex: Governor ?General of the Philippine Islands|High Commissioner to the Commonwealth of the Philippine Islands

lead.basis: The member's operative content is U.S. supervision of the Islands' government (EO 2456 places 'all matters pertaining to the Government of the Philippine Islands' under the War Department and directs the Governor General's reports there; EO 7447 delegates to the High Commissioner the Commonwealth's extradition business). Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directed the President to 'withdraw and surrender all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty then existing and exercised by the United States in and over the territory and people of the Philippine Islands', and Proclamation 2695 declared on July 4, 1946: 'The United States of America hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised by the United States of America in and over the territory and people of the Philippines'. Those words describe the class the member's content falls in; the reservations the statute and proclamation except are not the member's subject. For EO 7447, section 7 of the Act, under which the High Commissioner served, applies only 'Until the final and complete withdrawal of American sovereignty'. The date the instrument fixes is July 4, 1946 (ruling P5).

gaps: Earlier ends (the Governor General's office ended with the Commonwealth's inauguration on November 15, 1935; the Bureau of Insular Affairs moved to Interior under Reorganization Plan No. II of 1939) are not dated and their sources are not held.
EO 2456: the held text is signed September 19, 1916, the claim says September 16, 1916; settle identity from an official printing.

EO 7447 also authorizes U.S. diplomats and consuls abroad to act on Commonwealth extradition requests; that authority existed only for the Commonwealth and falls with it, but a reviewer should confirm.

procedure.description: EO 6858 (Textile Labor Relations Board), issued under Title I and Public Resolution 44.

lead.basis: The member's authority clause cites Title I and 'joint resolution approved June 19, 1934 (Public Resolution 44)', so EO 7076's Title I class does not alone account for it. EO 7084 (June 24, 1935) names it: 'The Textile Labor Relations Board created under Executive Order No. 6858 of September 26, 1934, and continued by Executive Order No. 7076 of June 15, 1935, is hereby further continued in existence until July 1, 1935'. That limit is disclosed; later extensions of the Board are not traced.

gaps: Trace later orders continuing the Textile Labor Relations Board after July 1, 1935 and Public Resolution 44's own period (48 Stat. 1183, not held).

procedure.description: NRA-typed orders that rest on another statute or authority (Title II public works, Public Resolution 44, corporation charters, the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act, the National Emergency Council's several statutes), or post-June 14, 1935 orders not reached by EO 7076 (EO 7120, 7192, 7252), or with no held text.

lead.basis: Neither EO 7076 nor NIRA sec. 2(c) reaches these orders by their terms: they rest wholly or partly on another statute, cite no Title I power, have no held text, or were issued after June 14, 1935 with a function that outlived April 1, 1936.

gaps: Each needs its own statute's lifecycle (Title II and its extensions; the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935; the Commodity Credit Corporation and Export-Import Bank statutes) or the PD-ADMIN organization rules.

EO 6651 has a second operative clause allocating $100,000 'from the appropriation of $3,300,000,000 authorized by section 220 of the National Industrial Recovery Act and made by the Fourth Deficiency Act', a Title II appropriation, so it is not only a Title I order.

procedure.description: Canal Zone-typed amendments of the general Civil Service Rules or schedules, and civil-service classification orders.

lead.basis: Civil Service Rules order; follows PD-CS-RULES. The order amends or applies the general Civil Service Rules, which operate beyond the Zone, so the end of the Canal Zone does not reach it by its terms.

gaps: Apply PD-CS-RULES.

procedure.description: Canal Zone-typed orders fixing pay or allowances of named persons (Isthmian Canal Commission members, the Board of Consulting Engineers, EO 595's dwelling and expenses for Lt. Col. Goethals).

lead.basis: Pay for named persons; follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (coordinator ruling P4) for the named-person entitlements, and needs the Panama Canal Act of 1912 (37 Stat. 560) for the Commission's discontinuance.

gaps: 37 Stat. 560 not held; tenures not traced.
EO 418: EO 474 (June 30, 1906) says 'All orders in conflict herewith are revoked'; a Wikisource editorial note lists EO 418 as revoked. Implied displacement under P3, disclosed only.
EO 595 only amends EO 577½ to give Goethals a furnished dwelling and expenses; under ruling P2 it would merge into EO 577½ (open, C1).

procedure.description: Canal Zone orders not decided: content reaching outside the Zone, Panama Railroad corporate matters, continuing individual rights, Commission organization, scanned texts, texts longer than the 12,000-character window, or orders whose subject is not Zone government alone.

lead.basis: The class event ends Zone-only government, but these orders reach outside the Zone (Panama City and Colon harbors, Washington offices), rest on Panama Railroad arrangements, create continuing individual rights (injury compensation, estates, deposits), concern the Isthmian Canal Commission's organization, or cannot be tested by the machine: their held text is a ProQuest scan (not graded for C3), runs past the 12,000-character window the engine reads, or contains words C3 excludes.

gaps: Per-member reasons are listed in the .md, section (d).

Later-law sources: Hull-Alfaro Treaty of 1936 for Panama and Colon sanitation; 37 Stat. 560 for the Isthmian Canal Commission; EO 474's 'All orders in conflict herewith are revoked' for EO 418 is implied displacement (P3), disclosed only.
